The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```java
coreNames = new ArrayList<String>(cores.keySet());
cores.clear();
```
Reason:
The original implementation retrieves the list of core names while holding a lock on the core list, and then clears the core map. This can lead to a race condition where cores are still being accessed or handed out to requests while they are being closed, resulting in potential inconsistencies and errors.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```java
coreList = new ArrayList<SolrCore>(cores.values());
cores.clear();
```
Reason:
The patch makes a temporary copy of the cores before clearing the core map, ensuring that the cores are not accessed concurrently while they are being closed. This prevents the race condition by isolating the core shutdown process from any ongoing requests that may try to access the cores.
